items.title: id: server-to-server file transfer (send) — #5345
items.body: Implements #5345 (transport + CLI/REPL slice of #1794, design #4975): a user-initiated, single-file copy from one running `id` server to another, performed by the source server with its own identity. ## What - **`transfer` module** (`pkgs/id/src/transfer.rs`): the one server-side transfer interface shared by every surface. Conflict pre-check over the meta protocol before any bytes move; bytes-before-name via the existing `push_and_name` (blobs push, then name registration, success only after the destination confirms); idempotent re-send (same hash already registered → `already_present`, nothing pushed); conflicts refuse by default, explicit replacement archives the existing destination file under `.archive.` first; the source is never modified. - **Meta protocol** (`/iroh-meta/3`, append-only per the compatibility rule): new `MetaRequest::Send` (discriminant 14, included in `is_write` so the source authorizes the initiating user with the existing write gate) and `MetaResponse::Send` receipt (discriminant 15). `wire_format_is_pinned` extended. `MetaProtocol` gains an optional endpoint; `id serve` and `LocalNode` wire the node's own endpoint in, so the destination authorizes the *source server's* node ID and records it as the copy's `origin` with its first-write `created` time (#4973/#5191 contract). - **CLI**: `id send SOURCE_NODE_ID NAME --to DEST_NODE_ID [--as DEST_NAME] [--replace]`. - **REPL**: `send [--replace] [DEST_NAME]`, sharing the same meta request. The web adapter stays #5346 and can call the same module/request; it is out of scope here. ## Tests Two-Iroh-node integration tests in `transfer.rs` (ephemeral `LocalNode`s, real QUIC + blobs + meta protocols): - send copies the blob, registers the name, and stamps the source server as `origin` with an upload time; source contents unchanged (copy, not move) - re-send is idempotent (`already_present`) - conflict refuses by default and changes nothing; `--replace` archives the old file under an archive name and registers the new hash - a destination whose write policy does not allowlist the source denies the send and gains no name Plus the extended wire-format pin test for the new protocol variants. ## Verification - `cargo check` in `pkgs/id`: pass - Targeted tests: `cargo test --lib -- transfer:: wire_format_is_pinned protocol:: meta_client:: fileops:: cli:: local::` in pkgs/id — all pass (4 two-node transfer tests, wire pin, CLI command-list coverage incl. README + module doc) Closes #5345 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: id(web): send selected files to another server (#5346)
items.body: Implements #5346, the web adapter for server-to-server file send. Its gate has cleared: issue #5345 closed with PR #7905 merged 2026-11-14, landing the shared `transfer` module this adapter calls. ## What - **`POST /api/files/send`** (`id-web`): the browser carries only references — file name, destination node ID, optional destination name and `replace` flag — and this server performs the transfer itself through `id_sync::transfer::send_file` with its own endpoint identity. No bytes through browser JavaScript. The 200 response is built from the transfer receipt, so success is shown only after the destination confirmed blob completion and name registration. - Structured errors: 400 empty name / invalid destination, 404 unknown file, 409 conflict (the transfer module refuses before any bytes move; retry with `replace` to archive + replace), 502 transfer failed (including an unallowlisted destination denying the send), 503 when the serving process wired no transfer endpoint. - Caller authorization is the web surface's own guard, as for every file-mutation route; the destination authorizes *this server* under its write policy, exactly as for the CLI/REPL path in #5345. - **Plumbing**: `AppState` gains `transfer_endpoint`; `id serve` passes its node endpoint through `web_routers_with_surface` (other constructors default to `None` → 503). `iroh` moves from dev-dependencies to dependencies of `id-web` (already in the lock via `id-sync`). - **UI**: the file-list bulk action bar gains a destination node ID input and a **Send to server…** action. `bulkSendToServer` posts one send per selected file and counts a file as sent only on an OK response carrying a well-shaped receipt (`isSendFileResponse`, the #7837 guard pattern) — failures are reported per file, never as success. - `WEB.md` route table updated. ## Tests - `cargo test -p id-web --lib send_file` — 6 passed: 400/503/404 validation, plus an in-process two-server probe *through the handler*: send copies the blob and registers the name on the destination (source untouched, copy not move), a retry returns `already_present`, a conflict refuses by default (409, destination untouched) and `replace` archives and lands, and an unallowlisted destination denies the send (502) and gains no name. Interruption safety is the transfer module's bytes-before-name ordering, covered by the #5345 tests in `pkgs/id/tests/transfer.rs`. - Full `cargo test -p id-web --lib`: 672 passed, 1 failed — `test_load_asset_urls_from_manifest`, which also fails on clean `main` in a bare worktree (web/dist manifest not built); unrelated to this change. - `vitest run src/file-op-responses.test.ts` — 13 passed. `tsc --noEmit` — pass. - Clippy was not run to completion locally: the pooled target dir mixes rustc 1.99.0 artifacts with the 1.99.1 clippy driver (E0514 on untouched crates). Queue task 9495 (lane code-d). Closes #5346. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added the ability to send selected files to another server by entering its node ID. * File transfers are handled server-to-server, with safeguards for unavailable destinations, missing files, and transfer conflicts. * Added a file transfer API endpoint and documented it. * Transfer responses include details about the destination and whether a file was already present or replaced.
